From 6c65cf23d4c6170fcf5714c32aa64689718cb142 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:01:35 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] batman-adv: tp_meter: avoid use of uninit sender vars

batadv_tp_recv_ack() and batadv_tp_stop() are only valid for tp_vars in the
BATADV_TP_SENDER role. When called with a BATADV_TP_RECEIVER role, it
proceeds to read sender-only members that were never initialized, leading
to undefined behavior.

This can be triggered when a node that is currently acting as a receiver in
an ongoing tp_meter session receives a malicious ACK packet.

Guard against this by checking tp_vars->role immediately after the
lookup and bailing out if it is not BATADV_TP_SENDER, before any of
those members are accessed.

Cc: stable@kernel.org
Fixes: 33a3bb4a3345 ("batman-adv: throughput meter implementation")
Reported-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>

diff --git a/net/batman-adv/tp_meter.c b/net/batman-adv/tp_meter.c
index ca6c3f6374bc..a3593d104caa 100644
--- a/net/batman-adv/tp_meter.c
+++ b/net/batman-adv/tp_meter.c
@@ -664,6 +664,9 @@ static void batadv_tp_recv_ack(struct batadv_priv *bat_priv,
 	if (unlikely(!tp_vars))
 		return;
 
+	if (unlikely(tp_vars->role != BATADV_TP_SENDER))
+		goto out;
+
 	if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tp_vars->sending) == 0))
 		goto out;
 
@@ -1101,12 +1104,16 @@ void batadv_tp_stop(struct batadv_priv *bat_priv, const u8 *dst,
 	if (!tp_vars) {
 		batadv_dbg(BATADV_DBG_TP_METER, bat_priv,
 			   "Meter: trying to interrupt an already over connection\n");
-		goto out;
+		goto out_put_orig_node;
 	}
 
+	if (unlikely(tp_vars->role != BATADV_TP_SENDER))
+		goto out_put_tp_vars;
+
 	batadv_tp_sender_shutdown(tp_vars, return_value);
+out_put_tp_vars:
 	batadv_tp_vars_put(tp_vars);
-out:
+out_put_orig_node:
 	batadv_orig_node_put(orig_node);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a vulnerability in the batman-adv throughput meter (tp_meter) implementation where two functions, `batadv_tp_recv_ack()` and `batadv_tp_stop()`, could be invoked with a `tp_vars` structure in the wrong role (`BATADV_TP_RECEIVER` instead of `BATADV_TP_SENDER`). This occurs when a node acting as a receiver receives a malicious ACK packet, causing the functions to read uninitialized sender-only fields and leading to undefined behavior.

### Modifications in `net/batman-adv/tp_meter.c`:

1. **`batadv_tp_recv_ack()`**:
   - Added a guard immediately after the `tp_vars` lookup:  
     ```c
     if (unlikely(tp_vars->role != BATADV_TP_SENDER))
         goto out;
     ```
   - This prevents any access to sender-specific members (e.g., `sending`) when the role is not sender. The existing `out` label already handles cleanup (release of references).

2. **`batadv_tp_stop()`**:
   - Added a similar role check:  
     ```c
     if (unlikely(tp_vars->role != BATADV_TP_SENDER))
         goto out_put_tp_vars;
     ```
   - Restructured the function’s exit labels to ensure proper reference counting:
     - The original single `out` label (which only released `orig_node`) was split into two labels:
       - `out_put_tp_vars`: releases the `tp_vars` reference.
       - `out_put_orig_node`: releases the `orig_node` reference.
     - The normal (sender) path now falls through to `out_put_tp_vars` after calling `batadv_tp_sender_shutdown()`, then to `out_put_orig_node`.
     - The early-exit for non-sender roles jumps to `out_put_tp_vars`, ensuring `tp_vars` is always freed (avoiding a memory leak that would have occurred with a simple `goto out`).

### Relationship between the changes:
Both modifications address the same root cause—accessing uninitialized sender-only data when the `tp_vars` role is `BATADV_TP_RECEIVER`. The change in `batadv_tp_recv_ack()` prevents the undefined behavior directly, while the change in `batadv_tp_stop()` not only prevents the undefined behavior but also fixes a resource leak (`tp_vars` reference) that would have been introduced if only a role check were added without adjusting the exit labels. Together, they ensure that both functions correctly bail out early without corrupting memory or leaking references when invoked in the wrong role.
